summary: Schwarzman Scholars is a fully funded one-year master's in Global Affairs at Tsinghua University in Beijing, covering tuition, room and board, travel, books, a laptop, insurance and a stipend. It selects young leaders (age 18–28) from all fields who show leadership, character, academic ability and openness to other cultures. The Class of 2027-28 window has closed; the next global round (Class of 2028-29) is expected to open in April 2027 and close in September 2027.
lookfor: Leadership: a record of leading people or initiatives, with impact
cycle: Class of 2028-29 (global applicants, non-Chinese citizens): application expected April–September 2027; interview invitations around mid-October; in-person interviews late October–early November 2027; programme starts August 2028. Exact dates are posted on the admissions page when the round opens.

eligibility.q: Will you be at least 18 and not yet 29 on 1 August 2028 (born after 1 August 1999)?
eligibility.no: The age rule has no exceptions. Consider Weidenfeld-Hoffmann (no age limit) or Chevening.

eligibility.q: Will you hold a bachelor's degree by 1 August 2028?
eligibility.no: Apply in a later round once your degree is completed.

eligibility.q: Are you a non-Chinese citizen with a regular passport (global track)?
eligibility.no: Chinese citizens apply on a separate China track with different dates.

eligibility.q: Can you show English proficiency (two years of English-taught post-secondary study, or TOEFL 100 / IELTS 7 / Duolingo 130 / Cambridge 185)?
eligibility.no: Most Nigerian, Ghanaian and Kenyan graduates studied in English and are waived. Otherwise, book a test well before the deadline.

eligibility.q: Can you travel to an in-person interview (e.g. London or New York) if shortlisted?
eligibility.no: Video interviews are offered only in very rare cases (serious health issues or visa denial). Plan for a visa early.

steps.title: Confirm eligibility and fit
steps.why: Schwarzman is a one-year leadership and global-affairs programme in China, not a technical master's. Fit with its mission matters.
do: Open the Schwarzman admissions page and read eligibility and selection criteria.
Check your date of birth against the age rule for the 2028 entry (born after 1 August 1999).
Read the FAQs on costs, interviews and English.
Write two sentences on why understanding China matters for your career.
tips: Selectors value curiosity about China and global affairs — not prior Mandarin.
avoid: Applying only for the money without a China-related purpose.
check: I meet age, degree and English rules, and I can explain why China.

steps.title: Attend an information session
steps.why: Sessions explain what the committee looks for and often include scholars' advice.
do: Open the information sessions page and register for an online session.
Prepare one question about the essays or interview.
Take notes on any updates to the essay prompts.
tips: Ask scholars from Africa about their path if possible.
avoid: Asking questions already answered in the FAQs.
check: I attended a session or watched a recording.

steps.title: Build a timeline and gather form information
steps.why: The form asks for many structured details; collecting them early leaves time for essays.
do: When the round opens (expected April 2027), create your account from the admissions page.
Prepare: up to five awards with why each matters; up to five leadership roles; up to two full-time jobs with achievements.
Note your passport details exactly; a valid passport is needed before enrolment.
Set dates: recommenders asked (-90), essays drafted (-45), final (-10), submit (-5).
tips: Choose leadership roles that show growth over time, not just titles.
avoid: Putting internships in the jobs section — they belong on your resume.
check: All form details are in one document.

steps.title: Get transcripts and English evidence
steps.why: Official transcripts from every institution are required; missing or locked files weaken your file.
do: Request official transcripts from every university you attended (registry or e-transcript portal).
Get English translations for any non-English documents.
Make sure each PDF opens without a password.
If your degree was not taught in English for two years, book TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Cambridge now.
tips: Ask your registry for a letter confirming English as the medium of instruction to support the waiver.
check: All transcripts open and are readable.

steps.title: Write a two-page resume
steps.why: The resume gives selectors a fast picture of your leadership and impact.
do: Keep to two pages maximum.
Sections: Education; Experience (include NYSC, internships, part-time work); Leadership; Awards; Skills and languages.
Each bullet: action + result with a number.
Save as PDF.
tips: Make the leadership section the strongest part.
check: Two pages, every bullet shows a result.

steps.title: Write the leadership essay
steps.why: Leadership is the first selection criterion; this essay is your main evidence.
do: Read the exact prompt in the 2027 application form.
Pick one leadership story with real stakes, where you made choices and others followed.
Structure: the situation; your decision and actions; obstacles; results with numbers; what you learned about leading.
End with how this shapes the leader you want to become.
Cut to 750 words or fewer.
tips: Show how you brought different people together — this links to intercultural competency.
avoid: Exceeding 750 words — essays over the limit may be disqualified.
Describing a group's success without your specific role.
check: One clear story with my role and measurable results; at most 750 words.

steps.prompt: Your demonstrated leadership and potential (see the exact prompt in the current application).

steps.title: Write the statement of purpose
steps.why: Selectors want to see why this programme in China is the right next step for your goals.
do: Read the exact prompt in the form.
Para 1: your long-term goal and the problem you want to address.
Para 2: why understanding China and global affairs is necessary for that goal.
Para 3: what you will contribute to the cohort and take from the programme.
Cut to 500 words or fewer.
tips: Link a specific China connection (trade, infrastructure, technology, climate) to your country's context.
avoid: Generic praise of China or Tsinghua.
check: Clear goal, clear China link, at most 500 words.
steps.prompt: Your career aspirations and why Schwarzman Scholars fits them (see the exact prompt in the current application).

steps.title: Answer the two short questions
steps.why: Short answers show personality and range in very few words.
do: Read both prompts in the current form (they can change each year).
Write one specific idea per answer — no introductions.
Keep each to 100 words or fewer.
tips: Use these to show something not covered elsewhere (a value, a curiosity, a culture).
check: Each answer is specific and at most 100 words.
steps.prompt: Two short-answer questions set in the current application.

steps.title: Record the one-minute video
steps.why: Optional but highly recommended: it lets selectors meet you before interviews.
do: Write a 130–150 word script: who you are, what drives you, why Schwarzman.
Record in a quiet, well-lit place, facing the camera; keep to one minute.
Upload to YouTube or Vimeo as 'Unlisted' (not private, no password) and paste the link in the form.
Open the link in a private browser window to check it works.
tips: Speak naturally; one take that sounds like you beats a polished script.
avoid: Setting the video to Private — reviewers cannot see it.
check: Video is one minute and the unlisted link works.

steps.title: Secure three recommenders
steps.why: Letters must confirm your intellect, character and leadership with specific examples.
do: Pick three people who know you well: e.g. a lecturer, a work supervisor, and a leader from a community project.
Ask 8–10 weeks before the deadline; send your resume, essay drafts and the three criteria to cover.
Enter their emails in the form; the system sends each a unique upload link.
Remind them two weeks and three days before the deadline — late letters are not reviewed.
tips: Ask each recommender to focus on a different strength with one concrete story.
avoid: Sending letters by email or paper — only the portal is accepted.

steps.title: Complete the form and submit
steps.why: Submissions are final: you cannot reopen the application to edit.
do: Fill every section: personal info (exactly as on passport), education, languages, essays, video, experience, awards, leadership, recommenders.
Choose your anticipated interview location (e.g. London late October or New York early November).
Add a clarification comment only if something needs explaining (e.g. a grade dip during ASUU strike).
Proofread, type your full legal name as e-signature and submit. There is no application fee.
tips: Submit a few days early in case of upload problems.
avoid: Sending extra materials (writing samples, extra letters) — the programme discourages them.

steps.title: Plan interview travel and visa early
steps.why: Interviews are in person; the programme pays travel and one hotel night, but you need a visa for the interview city.
do: If you chose London, check whether you need a UK Visitor visa and how long processing takes in Lagos, Abuja or your city.
Consider applying for the visa before you hear about shortlisting if processing is slow.
Keep your passport valid and available.
tips: Choose the interview city where you are most likely to get a visa in time.
avoid: Waiting for the invitation (mid-October) before thinking about a visa.
check: I know my visa route for the interview city.

Watch: Schwarzman Scholars Interview Day Guide Part 1 | Prep, Panel & What Nobody Tells You (faye days)

steps.title: Prepare for the panel interview
steps.why: Panels of leaders from business, government and academia test your thinking, leadership and openness.
do: Re-read your whole application.
Prepare clear answers on: your leadership story, your goals, why China, a current issue in China–Africa or China–world relations.
Read a week of global news, including Chinese perspectives.
Do two mock interviews with people who will challenge you.
tips: Show you can hold a view and still listen to the opposite one.
check: I can discuss a current global issue from more than one perspective.

steps.title: Accept the offer and prepare for China
steps.why: Successful scholars must finish their degree by 1 August and obtain a Chinese student visa.
do: Accept the offer by the stated date.
Complete your degree and send final documents.
Apply for the Chinese student visa using the programme's documents.
Start basic Mandarin practice before arrival.
tips: Keep in touch with the scholar community early.
check: Offer accepted and visa plan ready.

faq.q: Do I need to speak Mandarin?
faq.a: Mandarin is not listed among the eligibility requirements; the application and programme are in English.
No fixed minimum, but academic excellence is expected — successful applicants are usually among the top of their class.
No. The Class of 2027-28 window has closed. The next global round is expected to open in April 2027.
The programme covers interview travel and one hotel night.
